problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a critical circuit for its fleet of autonomous drones, tasked with collecting environmental sensor data from ten distinct monitoring stations positioned across a remote archipelago. The geographic coordinates of each station are precisely recorded as follows:  
Station Alpha: (154,59)  
Station Beta: (36,47)  
Station Gamma: (116,28)  
Station Delta: (122,88)  
Station Epsilon: (181,66)  
Station Zeta: (33,7)  
Station Eta: (53,92)  
Station Theta: (85,121)  
Station Iota: (74,75)  
Station Kappa: (141,162)  

The flight distances between stations, measured in kilometers, are predetermined and immutable:  
Alpha to Gamma: 49.0 km  
Alpha to Delta: 43.2 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 27.9 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 131.7 km  
Alpha to Eta: 106.3 km  
Alpha to Theta: 92.8 km  
Alpha to Iota: 81.6 km  
Alpha to Kappa: 103.8 km  
Beta to Gamma: 82.2 km  
Beta to Delta: 95.3 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 146.2 km  
Beta to Zeta: 40.1 km  
Beta to Eta: 48.1 km  
Beta to Theta: 88.8 km  
Beta to Iota: 47.2 km  
Beta to Kappa: 155.7 km  
Gamma to Delta: 60.3 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 75.3 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 85.6 km  
Gamma to Eta: 89.8 km  
Gamma to Theta: 98.0 km  
Gamma to Iota: 63.0 km  
Gamma to Kappa: 136.3 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 63.0 km  
Delta to Zeta: 120.3 km  
Delta to Eta: 69.1 km  
Delta to Theta: 49.6 km  
Delta to Iota: 49.7 km  
Delta to Kappa: 76.4 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 159.3 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 130.6 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 110.6 km  
Epsilon to Iota: 107.4 km  
Epsilon to Kappa: 104.0 km  
Zeta to Eta: 87.3 km  
Zeta to Theta: 125.3 km  
Zeta to Iota: 79.4 km  
Zeta to Kappa: 188.9 km  
Eta to Theta: 43.2 km  
Eta to Iota: 27.0 km  
Eta to Kappa: 112.4 km  
Theta to Iota: 47.3 km  
Theta to Kappa: 69.4 km  
Iota to Kappa: 109.8 km  

Due to persistent signal interference, a direct flight corridor between Station Alpha and Station Beta cannot be utilized. Furthermore, owing to a regulatory mandate concerning airspace allocation, the final flight plan must incorporate exactly one—and not both—of the following two designated corridors: the link between Station Beta and Station Gamma, or the link between Station Gamma and Station Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-loop trajectory, wherein each monitoring station is visited exactly once before the drone returns to its origin, thereby minimizing the total flight distance.
